page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.10xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 40 dedicated physical cores and 40 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a baseline clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.4 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate stable compute performance across single-core and multi-core workloads. The instance achieved a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1439.29 and a multi-core score of 38381.56. In memory bandwidth testing, the system recorded 2132.58 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, which drops to 105.52 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and 36.66 GB/sec for large-block writes. Cryptographic and compression capabilities are supported by AVX-512 and AES instruction sets, reflected in a Passmark CPU encryption test score of 17670.65 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 25.14 GB/sec.

With a high density of dedicated compute cores relative to memory, this instance is structured for CPU-bound tasks rather than memory-intensive databases. It is well-suited for software compilation, web serving, and moderate-scale parallel processing, as indicated by a Geekbench clang compilation score of 28295.0 and a static web serving throughput of 23.2 GB/sec. The absence of local storage and GPUs represents a design tradeoff, optimizing cost efficiency for workloads that require raw CPU execution without the overhead of specialized hardware accelerators or high-capacity local NVMe drives.
